p1.original: 1.1 心理学是一个广阔的领域，包括许多专业方向，但从根本上说，心理学是一门研究行为和心理过程的科学。
p1.en: 1.1 Psychology is a broad field, encompassing many professional directions, but fundamentally it is a science of behaviour and psychological processes.

p2.original: 1.2 现代心理学由6个主要视角构成，它们是生物视角、认知视角、行为视角、全人视角、发展视角和社会文化视角，每个视角都发展出了有关心智和行为的全新概念。
p2.en: 1.2 Modern psychology consists of six main perspectives: biological, cognitive, behavioural, human, developmental and sociocultural, each of which has developed a whole new concept of mental and behavioural.

p3.original: 1.3 心理学家和其他学科的科学家一样，使用科学方法来实证性地检验他们的观点。
p3.en: 1.3 Psychologists, like scientists in other disciplines, use scientific methods to test their views empirically.

p4.original: “孩子们吃掉了各种各样的甜食——蛋糕、冰淇淋和糖果——之后，他们又蹦又跳，亢奋得像要疯掉了！”一位朋友在描述她8岁女儿的生日聚会时这样说道。
p4.en: "The children ate all kinds of sweet foods -- cake, ice cream and candy -- and then they jumped and jumped, and they were as high as they were going crazy! A friend said this when describing her 8-year-old daughter's birthday party.

p5.original: 当时我的脸上一定写满了怀疑，因为她突然停下来问：“你不信吗？”她又接着补充，“你们心理学家就是不相信常识，是吧？”
p5.en: My face must have been filled with suspicion because she suddenly stopped and said, "Don't you believe it? And she added, "You psychologists just don't believe in common sense, do you?

p6.original: 于是我回应她，人们认为的“常识”可能是错的，我举了人们曾以为“地球是平的”这件事为例。我还暗示她：“或许可能又错了——这次是人们只愿意相信他们看到的所谓的‘糖会让孩子们亢奋’。”
p6.en: So I responded to her that the idea that common sense might be wrong, and I took as an example the idea that the Earth was flat. And I also hinted at her: "Maybe it's wrong again -- this time people just want to believe that what they see is that sugar makes the kids so excited."

p7.original: “可能只是聚会让孩子们亢奋。”我补充道。
p7.en: "Maybe it's just a party that gets the kids excited. I added:

p8.original: “只愿意相信他们看到的？”我的朋友几乎喊叫起来，“你能证明糖不会让孩子变得亢奋吗？”
p8.en: "Only believe what they see? My friend almost hollered, "Can you prove that sugar doesn't make the baby so excited?

p9.original: “不能，科学不是那样运作的。”我谨慎地说，“但我能做的，就是做个实验来检验糖能让孩子‘亢奋’的说法，然后我们就能知道你的断言是否成立。”
p9.en: “No, science does not work that way. And I say, "But what I can do is do an experiment to test the way sugar makes a child ecstasy, and then we'll know if your assertion is true.

p10.original: 显然，当时不是和她探讨科学实验的最好时机，所以，让我把这个问题交给你吧。
p10.en: Obviously, it was not the best time to discuss scientific experiments with her, so let me leave this to you.

p11.en: This chapter considers the following topics:

p12.original: 心理学家会如何检验糖使儿童亢奋的说法？
p12.en: How would psychologists test the claim that sugar makes children exult?

p13.original: 我们邀请你思考一下该如何设计这个实验。比如，我们可以给孩子们一杯高糖饮料，看看会发生什么。但由于人们通常只会看到他们期望看到的事情，我们对糖和亢奋的预期很容易影响我们的观察。那么，我们如何设计一个关于糖和亢奋的实验，同时又不让它受到我们预期的影响呢？这不是一个容易解决的问题，但我们会一起思考，到本章结束时，你会得到解决这一问题的各种方法。
p13.en: We invite you to think about how to design this experiment. For example, we can give the kids a high sugar drink and see what happens. But because people usually only see what they expect, our expectations of sugar and excitement can easily influence our observations. How, then, do we design an experiment on sugar and excruciatingness without allowing it to be affected by what we expect? This is not an easy problem, but we will think together that by the end of this chapter you will have the means to resolve it.

p14.original: 本书的每一章都将以类似的问题开篇——希望它能让你积极地投入对心理学的学习，并且批判性地思考该章中的一些重要概念。通过和我们一起解决问题，而不仅仅是被动地阅读，这样才能让这些概念对你而言更有意义，也更容易记住（感谢记忆心理学，让我们知道的确如此）。
p14.en: Each chapter of the book will start with a similar question — hopefully it will allow you to actively engage in the study of psychology and critically reflect on some of the important concepts in the chapter. By working with us to solve problems, not just by reading them passively, these concepts can be made more meaningful to you and easier to remember (thank memory psychology, let us know that it is).

p15.original: “糖与亢奋”问题所阐述的重要概念是心理学最基本的概念之一：运用科学方法来探索心智和行为。但在我们深入探讨科学方法的细节之前，让我们先阐明心理学这个术语本身的含义。
p15.en: One of the most fundamental concepts of psychology is the important concept articulated by the issue of sugar and high spirits: the application of scientific methods for the exploration of mentalities and behaviour. But before we go into the details of the scientific approach, let us clarify the meaning of the term psychology itself.
